selection.rationale: Measured facts. (1) Objective split: ORIGINAL baseline end_to_end_ms 690.12 with ttft_ms 24.05 and decode_ms 666.12 (inputs/project.json), so 96.5% of the objective is the 31 decode steps at decode-phase Qwen3ForCausalLM call 323bcbe006b343648b346af9 (group 3e293c00b1fb98fbe29f, 374.18 ms inclusive diagnostic CUDA over 31 invocations), while the ttft_ms constraint at <=1.05x fresh ORIGINAL TTFT is decided entirely in the prefill span at prefill-phase Qwen3ForCausalLM call 900c23e99c808d2c9bda215a (group e0861b46dbeeb562f67f, 21.57 ms diagnostic CUDA; adapter _infer, inputs/adapter.py:33-38). Decode is host-dispatch bound: execution_timeline (revision b61996e1, inputs/observations/current/execution_timeline-1221e205.json) measured a 1441.75 ms profiled window with only 386.81 ms kernel-active union and 1054.37 ms gaps; python_runtime counted ~546 Python module dispatches per forward (17,472 _wrapped_call_impl over 32 forwards, inputs/observations/current/python_runtime-aea48e29.json). (2) The previous candidate at exactly the decode boundary (inputs/previous-candidate/candidate.py, per-length CUDA graphs with capture-blind is_tracing, static K/V masters, bitwise build verification) PASSED full quality (max_abs_error 0.0 on 4,861,988 compared elements across both continuous steps, exact greedy tokens, teacher replay exact) and cut decode_ms 666.12->368.41 and end_to_end_ms 690.12->395.01, but was REJECTED solely for fixed_diagnostic_original_TTFT_constraint_failed: candidate ttft_ms 26.51 (unobserved, samples 26.31-26.70) and 25.92 (observed, samples 25.79-26.01) vs limit 25.2536 (=1.05x24.051052), while the same-day original measured 23.97-24.59 (inputs/previous-feedback.txt; terminal-audit endpoints 0-B/1/2). The regression is systematic (+2.0-2.5 ms in all 10 candidate samples, present in the first repeat after warmup), even though prefill ran the untouched parent - it is an interaction of retained setup state and/or the now gap-free, GPU-saturated 368 ms decode replay with the next invocation's prefill span, not direct code cost; warm-run allocation counters are constant across samples, so which mechanism (allocator layout vs power/boost-clock state) dominates remains an explicit unknown. (3) That failure cannot be repaired from the decode boundary alone: nothing inside the decode phase lies inside the ttft_ms span, which ends at the first-token torch.cuda.synchronize() before any decode step. The original TTFT span carries ~2.4 ms of host overhead over prefill kernel time (24.05 ms wall vs 21.57 ms prefill CUDA busy) that is reclaimable only by owning the prefill boundary. (4) The two edits need one another: the decode graphs already read their 256-token prefix through self-owned static masters refreshed from each invocation's prefill cache, so adding a prefill replacement that writes those same masters directly (and returns a view-mirror request-scoped cache plus cloned logits) is one coherent state-ownership protocol, one bundle, verified by one bitwise build procedure - a joint candidate, with legacy direct-callable module boundaries at both phase calls and no functional dispatch installed. All calls in both selected groups are included in affected_calls, which is the union of both module subtrees (26,868 calls: prefill root + 3,641 descendants, decode root + 23,225 descendants, disjoint), matching the convention of the previous accepted-structure selection at this boundary.
selection.hypothesis: Repair the only observed failure (ttft_ms constraint) by extending the quality-proven, bitwise-verified CUDA-graph machinery from the decode steps to the prefill+first-token span, while keeping the 31 per-cache-length decode graphs exactly as validated. At build(context), after the existing master-buffer construction, additionally capture ONE prefill graph on the workload's own GPU-resident input tensor (fixed (1,256) int64, same object every invocation, guarded by data_ptr/shape with plain-parent fallback), under the same capture-blind is_tracing patch and with the same per-build BITWISE verification of logits and all 36 layers' K/V against an eager parent prefill; any mismatch permanently disables graphs and falls back to the parent (quality preserved, speedup lost, never silent numerics). At invocation time the prefill boundary replays the graph, writing positions 0..255 of the shared K/V masters directly (eliminating the previous first-decode-step refresh copies) and returning cloned last-position logits plus a view-based request-scoped DynamicCache mirror, so each invocation still recomputes all state from the current input and nothing from a prior invocation is read. Expected effect, to be tested by the framework's fresh measurement: TTFT drops by the ~2.4 ms host launch/alloc overhead of the eager prefill span (24.05->~22.0 if the regression was host-side; ~23.8-24.1 even if the whole +2.3 ms regression was a ~10% kernel slowdown from post-replay clock state), restoring ttft_ms <= 25.25 against a ~24.05 fresh original with margin in either case, while end_to_end_ms stays ~391-395 ms (vs 690.12 original, 43% improvement; decode_ms unchanged at ~368.4 plus a small gain from the removed refresh copies). Secondary benefit: prefill replay cannot perturb the caching allocator during the TTFT span, removing the allocator-layout half of the unknown. Testable predictions: (a) fresh evaluator TTFT median <= 1.05x fresh original TTFT across all repeats; (b) full logits and exact-token checks still pass bit-for-bit through greedy and teacher-forced replays (graph_replay route labels at both boundaries); (c) if the prefill build verification fails, the candidate falls back to parent prefill and reproduces the known 26.5 ms TTFT failure rather than corrupting quality - that outcome falsifies the repair and leaves quality intact. Risks kept explicit: prefill SDPA runs the is_causal path whose capture behavior must match eager (verified per build, else fallback); the ttft_ms constraint baseline is the evaluator's fresh measurement, so margin, not equality, is the target.
